item.text:
Every first-version requirement is covered below. Ticket labels are provisional; Storybloq will assign IDs after approval.

| Requirement | Source | Coverage | Acceptance evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| List and add books | README “Status”; `src/books.js`, `src/server.js` | **E1**—existing functionality | Source inspection confirms list/add endpoints. Tests have not been run. |
| Find books by title or author | README; your correction to plan missing search | **A2**, reviewed at **C1** | Search matches either field; blank search lists all books; empty and no-result states are clear. |
| Lend a book to a pupil | Your first-version requirements | **B1** API, **B2** interface, demonstrated at **C2** | Teacher selects a copy, enters a pupil label and due date, and sees the active loan. A copy cannot have two active loans. |
| Record a return | Your first-version requirements | **B1**, **B2**, **C2** | Return persists, frees the copy, and remains recorded. Repeating a return does not change its original timestamp. |
| See overdue books | Your first-version requirements; README “Still to do” | **B3**, **C2** | Outstanding overdue loans show book, pupil label, and due date. Returned loans disappear; date boundaries are tested. |
| Lose nothing on restart | Your first-version requirements | **A1** storage, **B1** loan persistence, **D1** integrated verification | Books, identifiers, active loans, due dates, and recorded returns survive restart. Failed or uncertain saves have explicit recovery behavior. |
| One teacher uses the app; pupils do not | Your users statement | **A1**, **A2**, **B2**, **B3** | Teacher-facing local interface supports the whole journey without pupil accounts. |
| Keep existing technology | Your technology instruction; `package.json` | All implementation tickets | Retain dependency-free Node.js and JavaScript; use built-in filesystem storage and plain browser assets. |
| Accept the complete first version | Your combined outcomes | **C3**, following **C2** and **D1** | Teacher reviews the working journey, restart evidence, and operating instructions. |

The following are **proposed implementation choices**, made under your instruction to use judgment—not additional requirements attributed to you:

| Choice | Responsible tickets |
|---|---|
| One book record represents one physical copy | A2, B1, B2 |
| Editable 14-day loan default; overdue starts the day after the due date, using local calendar dates | B1, B2, B3 |
| Single local process, loopback access, and protection against cross-site requests | A1 |
| JSON storage with atomic writes, retry identification, and recovery after uncertain saves | A1, B1, D1 |
| Remove pupil labels on return while preserving return records; explain residual data in old backups | B1, B2, D1 |
| Keyboard-accessible controls, safe text rendering, and loading/error/retry states | A2, B2, B3 |
| Document startup, testing, backup, restore, and recovery | D1 |

Fines, reservations, reminders, reports, pupil accounts, multiuser access, and cloud deployment are outside this first version. No requirement is waiting on an unresolved owner decision.

**C1** reviews the catalogue interface, **C2** demonstrates circulation, and **C3** accepts the first version. These are ordinary checkpoint tickets; their closure is not technically restricted to owner approval.

Inspection changes nothing in the proposed package. Its quality level remains **Full pipeline**, and the captured review status is unchanged.
